content.text: I read the release and checked every figure, period and basis in the brief against it.

facts.evidence: Net revenue increased 14% to $11.6 billion, or 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion, or $2.97 per share, representing a 7% and 10% increase, respectively, over the prior year.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion, or $3.32 per share, representing an 8% and 11% increase, respectively, over the prior year.
Service revenue grew 14% to $4.9 billion, while data processing revenue rose 17% to $6.0 billion. (the brief does not label it the largest category, but the figure, period and basis are correct)
GAAP operating expenses rose 19% to $4.8 billion, primarily driven by personnel expenses and special items.
Payments volume increased 10% on a constant-dollar basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026. / Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions grew 12% on a constant-dollar basis
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities totaled $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
Monitor the impact of the $563 million in severance costs and $237 million litigation provision associated with the interchange multidistrict litigation case on future operating expenses.
International transaction revenue increased 6% to $3.9 billion (the brief does not note it was the slowest category, but the figure, period and basis are correct)

claims.claim: Fiscal Q3 2026 GAAP net income was $5.6 billion.
Fiscal Q3 2026 GAAP earnings per share were $2.97.
GAAP net income increased 7% over the prior year.
GAAP earnings per share increased 10% over the prior year.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.32.
Non-GAAP net income increased 8% over the prior year.
Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 11% over the prior year.
Net revenue increased 14% to $11.6 billion.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP operating expenses rose 19% to $4.8 billion.
The GAAP operating expense increase was primarily driven by personnel expenses and special items.
claims.note: The release attributes the 19% increase 'primarily driven by an increase in personnel expenses' only; special items are described as included in GAAP opex, not as a driver of the increase. In fact the litigation provision special item fell year over year ($615M prior year vs $237M current year), so naming special items as a driver of the increase is not supported.

claims.claim: Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 17% to $3.9 billion.
The non-GAAP operating expense increase was driven by marketing and personnel expenses.
Service revenue grew 14% to $4.9 billion.
Data processing revenue rose 17% to $6.0 billion.
International transaction revenue increased 6% to $3.9 billion.
Other revenue rose 45% to $1.5 billion.
Payments volume increased 10% on a constant-dollar basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions grew 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Total cross-border volume increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
The release does not provide specific financial guidance or outlook figures for future periods.
Management commented that consumer and business spending remains resilient.
Management commented that the strategy continues to deliver strong performance across consumer payments, commercial, and money movement solutions.
The company stated it is designing, building, and shipping products at an increased velocity to position itself to capture opportunities ahead.
Visa repurchased approximately 14.5 million shares of class A common stock for $4.9 billion during the quarter.
Visa had $28.4 billion of remaining authorized funds for share repurchases as of June 30, 2026.
The board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.670 per share of class A common stock, payable on September 1, 2026.
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities totaled $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
Visa deposited $250 million into its litigation escrow account on June 25, 2026.
The escrow deposit has the same economic effect on earnings per share as repurchasing class A common stock.
Fiscal Q3 2026 results included $563 million of severance costs.
Fiscal Q3 2026 results included a $237 million litigation provision associated with the interchange multidistrict litigation case.
Other revenue growth of 45% and data processing revenue growth of 17% exceeded the 14% growth in net revenue.
$4.9 billion of share repurchases were spent in the current quarter.
